body.p: Regarding the above-mentioned technical features, the present application uses "ring- shaped photosensitive surface" for obtaining the light intensity value, it is obvious that the "ring- shaped photosensitive surface" is a light receiving device of the photodetector.

However, D1 recites in its specification that, "the coupling system 2203 can couple light from the light source to the incident fiber bundle of the fiber optic probe 2205 (e.g. 1001 in Figure 10), which can guide the light to the measured medium 2207. Therefore, the detection fiber bundles in the fiber optic probe 2205 (such as two or more of 1003, 1005, and 1007 in Figure 10) can guide the diffuse reflected light of the measured medium 2007 to the processing device 2209. The processing device 2209 may include a detector 2209-1 (e.g. a photodetector) to detect optical signals from the fiber optic probe and convert them into electrical signals for further processing".
It is obvious that the "fiber" in D1 is completely different from the "ring-shaped photosensitive surface" in the present application.

Further, D1 is silent about any content related to the number, the inner diameter, the ring width of the "ring-shaped photosensitive surface". Therefore, D1 does not disclose the above technical features.

p.u: does not teach the above technical features.

body.p: First, Applicant submits it is nonobvious to use the ring-shaped photosensitive surface to fully reflect the impact of uncontrollable changes.

In the process of realizing the inventive concept of the present application, it is found that in the non-invasive detection of tissue components, uncontrollable interference caused by human physiological changes (for example, muscle shaking) and other reasons will affect the detection. Such uncontrollable interference may cause changes in the intensity and direction of the outgoing light at the outgoing position at a certain distance from the incident position, and such changes are vectorial for the incident position of the light. That is, it is related to the position and direction of the outgoing light, and the intensity of the interference and the outgoing direction (that is, the outgoing direction of the light toward the space) are random. These changes are among main reasons that affect the non-invasive detection accuracy of living body components.

Differential detection is an effective method to eliminate the impact of uncontrollable interference on signals. To eliminate the impact of uncontrollable interference through differential detection, it is required that the interference is reflected in the synchronous change of two signals participating in differential operation, that is, the common mode of interference. This is based on the premise that the change of light intensity received by a single photosensitive surface may well reflect the impact of uncontrollable interference. Additionally, the uncontrollable interference caused by human physiological changes is vectorial. Therefore, an effective average effect is required to ensure that the change of light intensity received by the single photosensitive surface may well reflect the impact of human physiological changes, that is, the impact of uncontrollable interference may be reflected by the single light intensity change through sufficient average effect. For a better understanding, the light source drift of non-physiological changes is taken as an example to briefly explain. For example, if the intensity of the light source changes by 1%, if the light intensity is received only through several points at different angles distributed at the same distance from the incident light spot, the total light intensity received by the optical fiber bundle (the essence of sum is average) is difficult to accurately reflect that the light intensity changes by 1%. This is because optical fiber reception is discrete reception, and the human tissues are unevenly distributed and have physiological changes. However, if the reception of several points turns into a ring-shaped surface reception (which can be understood as a ring-shaped photosensitive surface), especially if the ring-shaped surface also has a certain area, the total light

intensity received by the photosensitive surface may more accurately reflect that the light intensity changes by 1%.Therefore, if the method of D1 is adopted (see paragraphs [0194], [0204], [0316] and [0317], FIGS. 37(a) - 37(d) of D1), that is, the ring-shaped optical fiber probe composed of multiple discrete optical fiber bundles being connected with the detector, and the ring-shaped optical fiber probe receives the light intensity value emitted from the surface of the tested part, transmits the light intensity value to the detector, and then the detector collects the light intensity value, then the change of light intensity received by the optical fiber will be difficult to reflect the impact of uncontrollable interference. This is because the optical fiber reception is unstable, and the optical fiber reception is only discrete reception at several angles. In addition, even if a certain method is used to stable the optical fiber reception, that is, to make the signal-to-noise ratio high, the average effect is not enough to reflect the impact of uncontrollable interference because the optical fiber reception is only a discrete reception at several angles.

On the basis of the above researches, the application proposes that the light intensity value emitted from the surface of the tested part may be received by means of continuously distributed photosensitive surfaces. This is because the continuous distribution of the photosensitive surface may achieve an essential improvement in the average effect, and the changes in light intensity received in this way may reflect the impact of uncontrollable interference. Among them, for the continuously distributed photosensitive surface, since the ring-shaped photosensitive surface may receive the light intensity value of the outgoing light from the 3600 range and may ensure the reception of the maximum range of light intensity values, the continuously distributed photosensitive surface may be a ring-shaped photosensitive surface.

Additionally, Applicant submits that since in the solution of D1, the detection for tissue components is achieved by using the ring-shaped fiber probe in combination with the detector, thus it is a completely different method from the solution of the present application.

Further, it should be noted that on the basis of D1, the only option considered by those skilled in the art to improve is in a direction of how to further modify the ring-shaped fiber probe, for example, increasing the signal-to-noise ratio. However, according to the above descriptions, increasing the signal-to-noise ratio is not an essential method to improve the differential detection
effect, thus, it is nonobvious for those skilled in the art to think of the receiving method by using the ring-shaped photosensitive surface.

Further still, Applicant submits that specific sizes of the ring-shaped photosensitive surface is nonobvious for those skilled in the art by referring the wavelength of incident light and the environment. In order to ensure that the change of light intensity received by the single photosensitive surface may reflect the influence of uncontrollable interference, it is necessary to ensure sufficient effective average effect, that is, the ring-shaped photosensitive surface must have a certain area. In this case, it is necessary to limit the ring width of the ring-shaped photosensitive surface. On this basis, in order to improve the non-invasive detection accuracy of tissue components, the application further finds that the inner diameter of two ring-shaped photosensitive surfaces and the spacing between the two are crucial.
Specifically, the inner diameter range and the ring width range of the ring-shaped photosensitive surface are defined based on the following considerations.

The inner diameter range of the ring-shaped photosensitive surface is required to be determined in combination with a transmission path of detection light for the tissue component to be detected. Take blood glucose as an example, since the dermis is the optimal target skin layer for extracting blood glucose signals, if the inner diameter of the ring-shaped photosensitive surface is too small, it will mainly receive the light transmitted in the epidermis. If it is too large, it will mainly receive the light transmitted in the subcutaneous fat layer.

The spacing between two ring-shaped photosensitive surfaces is required to be determined in combination with the common mode of interference and the sensitivity of differential signal to the tissue component to be detected. If the spacing between two ring-shaped photosensitive surfaces is smaller, the common mode of uncontrollable interference is better, and the effect of eliminating uncontrollable interference through differential detection is better. However, because differential detection will eliminate part of the blood glucose information, if the two are too close, the blood glucose information may be eliminated completely, which greatly reduces the sensitivity
of blood glucose detection. Therefore, the spacing between the two ring-shaped photosensitive surfaces is required to be moderate.

To this end, the present application proposes that using two ring-shaped photosensitive surfaces having suitable sizes and spacing to collect the light intensity value, so as to improve the common mode of the interference, and using differential calculation to reduce the common mode interference. Since it is necessary to improve the common mode of interference and ensure the sensitivity of differential signals to the tissue components to be measured, not a ring-shaped photosensitive surface of any size may meet the above requirements. It is necessary to determine the appropriate inner diameter range of the ring-shaped photosensitive surface and the ring-shaped width range of the ring-shaped photosensitive surface. In other words, the specific size of the ring- shaped photosensitive surface requires a lot of researches and creative work, which is not easy for those skilled in the art to set in combination with factors such as the wavelength of the incident light and the environment.

As such, claim 1 of the present application proposes that an inner diameter of each ring- shaped photosensitive surface is greater than or equal to 0.5mm and less than or equal to 6mm, and a ring width of each ring-shaped photosensitive surface is greater than or equal to 0.05mm and less than or equal to 0.3mm.

Additionally, it should be noted that, Applicant has been deeply involved in the field for nearly 30 years. Prior to the priority date of the application, on the one hand, no prior art related to the specific size of the ring-shaped photosensitive surface has been found in literature related to the detection of biological tissue composition (including patent literature and non-patent literature), and on the other hand, no ring-shaped photosensitive surface for the measurement of tissue composition has been found in specific products.

Thirdly, Applicant believes that the non-invasive blood glucose detection has been carried out using the ring-shaped photosensitive surface defined in independent claim 1 of the application, and the real blood glucose signal has been extracted from the human body, and the ideal technical effect has been obtained.

On one hand, according to the content recorded on pages 13 to 15 of the description of the priority application (CN201811539082.1) of the present application, "as shown in Figure 10 (in Figure 10, in order to clearly display the variation trend of differential light intensity at six wavelengths in the same figure at the same time, normalization processing is performed, that is, dividing by the mean value of differential light intensity at each wavelength) the change of differential light intensity may well track the change of blood glucose true value. Figure 11 is the result of partial least squares modeling and prediction, and the main parameters are listed in Table 4. RMSEC is the corrected root mean square error, RMSECV is the interactive verification root mean square error, R2 is the determination coefficient, and PCs is the number of hidden variables."

On the other hand, Applicant provides other experimental data to illustrate the technical effect of independent claim 1 of the application.See Fig. 1, Fig. 2, Fig. 3 and Table 1 Figure 1 shows the measurement results of a diabetes patient adjusting blood glucose through a single diet, which may be called the results of a single sugar load experiment. Figure 2 shows the results of a healthy volunteer through a single sugar loading experiment. Figure 3 shows the measurement results of another healthy volunteer adjusting blood glucose changes through two consecutive diets, which may be called the results of the double sugar load experiment. Table 1 shows the statistical results of 17 single sugar loading experiments.

Figures 1 to 3 and Table 1 show the detection data at the wavelength of 1550nm. Figures 1 to 3 show the changes of differential light intensity values (i.e. differential signals) (based on fasting blood glucose value, i.e. differential light intensity value of the first blood glucose value) and blood glucose measured values obtained by differential detection of the inner diameter of the ring-shaped photosensitive surface with 4.4mm and 3.8mm, 3.8mm and 3.2mm, 4.4mm and 3.2mm respectively. Table 1 shows the correlation coefficient R between the differential light intensity value obtained by differential detection of the inner diameter of the ring-shaped photosensitive surface with 4.4mm and 3.8mm respectively and the measured blood glucose value, as well as the root mean square error RMSE obtained by linear fitting. It is generally believed that the correlation coefficient between the differential light intensity value and the measured blood glucose value is higher than 0.8, which is a successful experimental result.
